Ruzhyn Jewish Сemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Zhytomyr Oblast, Ukraine

Not demolished. In the 1810s, R. Israel Friedman (1796–1850) — founder of the Ruzhin Hasidic dynasty, famous for his extravagant, almost royal court — established his seat in Ruzhyn. In 1838, he was accused of involvement in the murder of two Jewish police informers and held in custody for two years before being released under police surveillance; he left Ruzhyn in 1841, eventually settling in Sadhora (Sadigura) near Chernivtsi, documented elsewhere in this collection, where his line continued as the Sadigura Hasidic dynasty. Ruzhyn's own Jewish community reached 2,917 people (67 percent of the town) by 1897. In September 1941, 750 Jews were shot, and most of the remaining community, along with Jews from nearby settlements, was killed in a ghetto action in May 1942.
